name: Sicilian Najdorf
blurb: The most popular fighting answer to 1.e4. Black accepts a slightly passive position for rich counterplay; ...a6 is the move that defines the Najdorf.

ideas.e4 c5: Fights for d4 from the side and makes the position unbalanced, which gives both players real winning chances.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6: Covers e5 and opens a path for the c8 bishop.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4: Trades a side pawn for White's centre pawn, so Black ends up with more pawns in the centre.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6: Attacks e4, so White has to spend a move defending it.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6: The Najdorf move. It keeps White's pieces off b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...b5.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5: Lets the bishop come to e7, where it guards the f6 knight that White's g5 bishop is attacking.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2: Kicks the d4 knight and gains space. The d5 square gets weaker, so Black must keep watching it.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3: Kicks the knight from d4. Once it moves, Black can use ...Be6 to guard the d5 square.
The bishop covers d5, the hole that ...e5 left behind.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bc4: Blunts the c4 bishop, which was aiming at f7.
ideas.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 f4: Attacks the d4 knight and the f4 pawn at the same time.
